approved_compatibility_changes.reason: First version with CPython 3.14 wheels; original exact pin has no cp314 wheel.

22.0.0 was the first version with CPython 3.14 wheels (original exact pin 20.0.0 has no cp314 wheel). Further bumped 22.0.0 -> 23.0.1 to close CVE-2026-25087 (AWS Inspector2 finding against the published container image); 23.0.1 also ships cp314 wheels, confirmed via PyPI's published file listing for manylinux_2_28_x86_64 before relocking.
approved_compatibility_changes.verification: requirements-cpu.lock was regenerated with the documented regenerate_preserving_pins command (pyarrow's prior exact pin removed from the constraint input first, since an unmet exact pin there is otherwise unsatisfiable against pyproject.toml's own updated requirement); a full version diff of the regenerated lock against the prior one confirmed pyarrow is the only package whose resolved version changed. Reinstalled pyarrow==23.0.1 alone with hash verification inside the pinned target image and confirmed pyarrow.__version__ and a basic pa.table() round trip; the full 260-package environment and its 29 offline checks were not rerun since nothing else in the lock moved.

approved_compatibility_changes.reason: 2.14.3 subclasses pyarrow.PyExtensionType, removed in Arrow 21. 2.15.0 fixes that but fails importing HfFolder with the resolved Hugging Face Hub. 2.16.0 imports but Dataset.from_dict fails under Python 3.14. 4.1.0 first permits dill 0.4.0, but its own Pickler._batch_setitems(self, items) still rejects Python 3.14's additional obj argument. 4.1.1, 4.2.0 and 4.3.0 retain that signature. 4.4.0 changes it to accept *args and **kwargs; Dataset.from_dict, serial and multiprocess map, and to_pandas were executed successfully with Arrow 22.
approved_compatibility_changes.migration_caveat: This is a major-version dependency update. Datasets 4.x no longer supports dataset loading scripts; application-specific dataset loaders require integration review. No package or requested SEMOSS dependency was omitted.

approved_compatibility_changes.reason: 0.0.103 unconditionally requests its local-smart-turn-v3 extra, which pins onnxruntime~=1.23.2; that runtime has no cp314 wheel. It also pins numba==0.61.2, which has no cp314 wheel. All subsequent stable 0.x releases (0.0.104 through 0.0.108) retain onnxruntime~=1.23.2. 1.0.0 accepts onnxruntime~=1.24.3, numba>=0.61.2,<1 and soxr~=1.0.0, permitting cp314 wheels without dropping the smart-turn dependency.
approved_compatibility_changes.migration_caveat: Pipecat 1.0 removes TranscriptProcessor. The container applies the separately approved, exact-source-hash-guarded audio_compat.py patch to SEMOSS. Offline tests construct all three SEMOSS audio pipelines and verify user/assistant transcript event payloads. Live external audio/model/service integrations remain untested.

approved_compatibility_changes.reason: Closes CVE-2026-44716 (fixed in 1.2.0) and CVE-2026-54695 (fixed in 1.4.0), both AWS Inspector2 findings against the published container image. Reviewed the upstream changelog for the full 1.0.0-1.4.0 range: no change to the event names or construction pattern the SEMOSS audio_compat.py patch depends on (on_user_turn_stopped/on_assistant_turn_stopped); PipelineRunner's rename to WorkerRunner is a non-breaking deprecation (the old name still resolves as a subclass alias). onnxruntime/numba/soxr constraints are unchanged from 1.0.0, so the cp314-wheel availability this project depends on is unaffected.
approved_compatibility_changes.migration_caveat: Adds one new transitive dependency, pyyaml-include==1.4.1 (confirmed via a full lock diff: no other package's resolved version moved). Verified beyond the standard harness: patched a copy of py/audio/lk_to_pcat.py with the existing audio_compat.py (hash-guarded, unchanged), built the real python-dependencies image stage for linux/amd64 with pipecat-ai 1.4.0, and ran the project's own docker/il4/tests/check_audio.py against it inside that image - all three SEMOSS audio pipelines (speech_to_speech_realtime, listen_and_transcribe, listen_translate_and_transcribe) constructed correctly and the user/assistant transcript event payloads matched exactly. Only DeprecationWarnings surfaced (PipelineTask -> PipelineWorker, and several service constructors' positional kwargs in favor of a settings= object), none of which affect current behavior. Live external audio/model/service integrations remain untested.

approved_compatibility_changes.reason: Closes CVE-2026-96620 (CRITICAL, AWS Inspector2 finding against the published container image; fixed upstream in 0.2.121). Never left the 0.2.x line across all 153 published releases - no major/minor version boundary crossed.
approved_compatibility_changes.verification: requirements-cpu.lock regenerated (uv 0.11.17, matching install.sh's own venv/build-requirements/torch-backend-cpu/override sequence) with claude-agent-sdk, pipecat-ai (next entry) and fsspec (see below) the only pyproject.toml changes. Full lock diff reviewed line by line: ~70 other packages moved, all ordinary transitive churn across the gap since the lock was last generated, none touching a package SEMOSS's own py/ imports directly (confirmed via grep - no direct import of any package whose name changed, e.g. pyloudnorm->loudness, or crossed a major version, e.g. mcp 1.30.0->2.3.0). Reinstalled all 264 packages with --require-hashes --no-build-isolation inside the pinned target image (Annoy/pandasql/swifter source builds included) and ran uv pip check: all installed packages compatible.

approved_compatibility_changes.reason: Closes CVE-2026-102682 (MEDIUM, AWS Inspector2 finding; fixed upstream in 1.6.0). Stays within the 1.x line.
approved_compatibility_changes.verification: Same lock regeneration and full-diff review as the claude-agent-sdk entry above. Specifically re-verified the on_user_turn_stopped/on_assistant_turn_stopped event mechanism audio_compat.py depends on, since this is a 9-minor-version jump past the previously-reviewed 1.0.0-1.4.0 range: patched a copy of py/audio/lk_to_pcat.py with the existing audio_compat.py (hash-guarded, unchanged) and ran docker/il4/tests/check_audio.py against the freshly-installed 1.13.0 environment - all three SEMOSS audio pipelines constructed correctly and the transcript event payloads matched exactly (Ran 1 test ... OK). Only DeprecationWarnings surfaced, all '... removed in 2.0.0' (OpenAIRealtimeLLMService/OpenAISTTService's positional kwargs in favor of a settings= object, PipelineTask -> PipelineWorker) - pipecat-ai is still pre-2.0, so none affect current behavior, but a future 2.0.0 bump should expect these to become real breaks, not just warnings.

approved_compatibility_changes.reason: Not a version change - a pin-management gap found while regenerating the lock for the two entries above. fsspec had no explicit pin anywhere (not in pyproject.toml, overrides.in/.lock, or compatibility-constraints.in); 2023.10.0 in the prior lock was purely incidental, held down by some other package's then-current transitive constraint. Bumping claude-agent-sdk/pipecat-ai released whatever that was and fsspec resolved to 2025.10.0 - the exact ceiling datasets==4.4.0 allows - which would have silently broken fsspec_compat.py's hash guard (written against 2023.10.0's exact source) on the next unrelated lock regeneration.
approved_compatibility_changes.verification: Added "fsspec==2023.10.0" directly to pyproject.toml and re-regenerated; confirmed the lock returns to exactly 2023.10.0 and the applied_source_patches entry below still applies cleanly (hash guard unchanged, since it checks SEMOSS's own vendored source copy, not a value derived from fsspec's own package version).

approved_compatibility_changes.reason: Closes GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2 (CRITICAL, AWS Inspector2 finding against the published container image): certifi bundled the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root certificate, whose eight eMudhra intermediate CAs had compromised, revoked private keys, letting an on-path attacker with one of those keys issue valid-looking certificates for any hostname trusted by requests/urllib3/httpx/etc. GitHub's own advisory prose says "before 2026.10.18" (which would mean no action needed), but its structured vulnerable_version_range (>=2019.03.09, <2026.10.19) and first_patched_version (2026.10.19) both confirm 2026.10.18 - SEMOSS's prior pin - is still vulnerable; the prose is simply imprecise. 2026.10.23 is PyPI's actual latest release at the time of this fix, comfortably past the patch boundary either way. certifi carries no code, only CA trust data, so this is a pure data update with no API surface to break.
approved_compatibility_changes.verification: Hand-edited requirements-cpu.lock's certifi entry directly (version plus both hashes) instead of a full lock regeneration, after discovering the project's regenerate_preserving_pins command is not currently reproducible: even with zero certifi-related changes, a fresh resolve of the unmodified lock also reintroduces torchaudio (via langsmith, itself unchanged at 0.14.11) and a new lxml-html-clean (via lxml, itself unchanged at 6.1.3) - neither triggering package's own version moves, so something else's extras resolution evaluates differently today than when the committed lock was generated. Confirmed via a control run (the exact documented regenerate_preserving_pins command, touching nothing certifi-related) that this drift is unrelated to certifi and already present in the project's lock-regeneration process; reintroducing torchaudio in particular would silently undo its deliberate removal in an earlier fix. The two new hashes were independently verified two ways before use: uv's own --upgrade-package resolution, and PyPI's JSON API digests for certifi 2026.10.23's sdist and wheel directly - both matching exactly. certifi's "# via" dependents (httpcore, httpx, langchain-openai, msrest, requests, trafilatura) are unchanged. Verified against the BC-FIPS sibling repo by running its own install.sh + validate.py end to end against the identically hand-edited lock inside the pinned target image: certifi installed at 2026.10.23 with hash verification passing, uv pip check reported all packages compatible, all 29 validate.py checks passed, and neither torchaudio nor lxml-html-clean appeared. Applied the identical change here since both repos share the exact same requirements-cpu.lock content and certifi was byte-for-byte identical in both before this edit.
approved_compatibility_changes.unresolved: The lock-regeneration reproducibility gap itself (torchaudio/lxml-html-clean appearing on any fresh resolve regardless of what's being changed) is not fixed here - only certifi's own entry was hand-edited to avoid it. The next time someone runs a full regenerate_preserving_pins for an unrelated reason, this will resurface and needs its own investigation into which package's extras resolution changed.

applied_source_patches.reason: Closes CVE-2026-104851 / GHSA-27vj-qcqg-25rc (Server-Side Template Injection -> RCE in fsspec.implementations.reference.ReferenceFileSystem, CVSS 8.8), an AWS Inspector2 finding against the published container image. The upstream fix ships in fsspec 2026.6.0, but fsspec is a transitive-only dependency (via dask, datasets, huggingface-hub, torch) and datasets==4.4.0 caps it at fsspec[http]<=2025.10.0; reaching 2026.6.0 would require datasets>=5.1.0, which in turn requires pyarrow>=24.0.0 - reopening the pyarrow==23.0.1 pin that was carefully tuned for CPython 3.14 wheel availability and CVE-2026-25087 (see the pyarrow entry above). Forcing fsspec past datasets' own tested upper bound via an override, or taking the full datasets/pyarrow major-version chain, both carry materially more risk than the vulnerability itself once its actual reach is accounted for: the vulnerable code (CWE-94/CWE-1336) only triggers through ReferenceFileSystem's Kerchunk reference-JSON parsing, which SEMOSS does not use anywhere (confirmed: no reference to ReferenceFileSystem, kerchunk, or the reference:// protocol in py/). Applied the exact upstream fix instead, isolated to just the three vulnerable sinks, from fsspec commit 86438783 (PR #2039): unrestricted jinja2.Template(...).render(...) replaced with jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment().from_string(...).render(...) in _process_references1/_render_jinja, _process_templates, and _process_gen.
applied_source_patches.verification: Hash-guarded against fsspec 2023.10.0's exact reference.py source (same pattern as audio_compat.py); each of the three replacement blocks confirmed to occur exactly once, and the patched source compiles. Functionally verified twice: once in an ad hoc venv, and again inside the real built python-dependencies image for linux/amd64. Reproduced the advisory's own RCE proof-of-concept (a Kerchunk reference JSON with a 'gen' array whose templated key/url triggers jinja2.sandbox.SecurityError before the patch raises an unhandled exception) - unpatched fsspec 2023.10.0 fires the RCE (marker file created), patched fsspec raises jinja2.sandbox.SecurityError and creates no marker file. Also confirmed the advisory's documented benign case (plain '{{var}}' substitution) still resolves correctly, so legitimate Kerchunk usage is unaffected. The project's own validate.py (29 checks, 260 locked packages) passes unchanged since fsspec's version and public API are untouched.

accepted_vulnerabilities.summary: Path traversal via unsanitized file_name metadata in folder-based dataset builders (e.g. imagefolder/audiofolder); fixed upstream in 5.0.1.
accepted_vulnerabilities.reason_not_fixed: Reaching 5.0.1 requires pyarrow>=24.0.0, reopening the pyarrow==23.0.1 pin tuned for CPython 3.14 wheel availability and CVE-2026-25087 (same tradeoff as the fsspec entry above, and no smaller in-range fix exists this time - unlike fast-uri's parallel 3.x track, datasets has no backport; 5.0.1 is the actual minimum fix).
accepted_vulnerabilities.not_exploitable_because: The vulnerability requires two things in sequence: (1) loading a folder-based dataset whose file_name metadata is attacker-controlled, via datasets.load_dataset() with a folder builder (imagefolder, audiofolder, etc.), and (2) then calling save_to_disk() or push_to_hub() on it, which is the actual read-and-embed step. SEMOSS's only datasets usage (py/vector_database/faiss/_legacy_pickle_migration.py, py/legacy/legacy-3-18-25/gaas_simple_faiss.py, py/prototype/temporal_frame.py) is limited to Dataset.from_dict-style in-memory construction and concatenate_datasets; neither load_dataset with a folder builder nor save_to_disk/push_to_hub appears anywhere in the codebase (confirmed via grep across py/). Both gates the exploit depends on are absent, not just one.
accepted_vulnerabilities.reassess_if: A future use of datasets.load_dataset() with a folder-based builder (imagefolder/audiofolder/etc.) or a call to Dataset.save_to_disk()/push_to_hub() is introduced; either would reopen this as a live finding worth revisiting the pyarrow cascade for.

additional_constraints.reason: Python 3.14 changed the pickle._Pickler._batch_setitems signature; older permitted dill versions are not suitable. Datasets 4.4.0 supplies the corresponding custom Pickler fix.
Preserves upstream protobuf>=6.33.5 while also satisfying Pipecat 1.0's protobuf<7. The unconstrained upstream override selected 7.36.2 and pip check reported that incompatibility.

preservation.cpu_routing: Original explicit tool.uv.sources preserved. Installation uses uv --torch-backend cpu with PyPI as the default index, not a global extra-index fallback.
preservation.explicit_cpu_input: cpu.in repeats the three unchanged CPU extra requirements. The first compile using --extra cpu alone omitted torchaudio, so explicit inputs and an all-root-requirements coverage assertion were added. All three CPU packages are present in the final lock.

build.method: Hash-verified sdists, exact hash-locked build tools, --no-build-isolation, and portable Annoy compiler arguments. No package patching or --no-deps fallback. Build-only nose and wheel are removed by final lock synchronization.
build.reproducibility_limit: The Python input artifacts and build tooling are hash-locked. Locally built wheel byte hashes and OS repository snapshots are not locked; source hashes and compiler settings are recorded instead.

commands.regenerate_preserving_pins: uv pip compile pyproject.toml cpu.in --extra cpu --constraint requirements-cpu.lock --constraint compatibility-constraints.in --python /usr/bin/python3.14 --generate-hashes --emit-index-annotation --output-file requirements-cpu.lock --no-header
commands.regenerate_overrides: uv --no-config pip compile overrides.in --constraint requirements-cpu.lock --python /usr/bin/python3.14 --generate-hashes --output-file overrides.lock --no-header

includes: CPU-only torch calculation, torchaudio resampling, torchvision NMS, compiled Annoy indexing
